text: How an industrial arm is built: joints, degrees of freedom, work envelope, coordinate frames, tool center point, and interpolating joint and straight-line moves.
How industrial robots are programmed: online or offline, in RobotStudio and PolyScope, in vendor languages, and with ROS, which works with any vendor.
Why ROS exists: a common layer that works with any vendor for programming robots from different makers.
Choosing and sizing grippers, mounting, setting payload, and programming digital I/O to open, confirm grips, and talk to a PLC in URScript and RAPID.
How robot programs are organized (RAPID modules and routines, URScript functions and threads), recovering from missed picks, and a 3 by 3 palletizing loop.
Using cameras to pick parts not in a fixed place: 2D versus 3D guidance, camera mounting, lens and hand-eye calibration, and frame-shift math.
What open source is, making a first contribution, how robotics projects like ROS 2 and MoveIt work, and a real pull request lab.
Build a ROS 2 Lyrical Python package from scratch: workspaces, overlays, ros2 pkg create, setup.py, package.xml, rosdep, colcon, and driving Turtlesim in a square.
Planning arm motions with MoveIt 2 on ROS 2 Lyrical: URDF, SRDF, ros2_control mock hardware, move_group, OMPL, Pilz PTP/LIN, and a UR5e in RViz.
Where AI is used as of October 2026 (learned vision, predictive maintenance, LLM coding assistants, research foundation models), AI-written code evidence, and pre-motion checks.
How robots make smooth setpoints: trapezoidal, triangular, S-curve profiles, cubic and quintic time scaling, joint, linear, circular interpolation, zones, and MoveIt time parameterization.
Full math of a planar two-link arm: forward kinematics, the reachable ring, closed-form inverse kinematics with atan2, rounding edge cases, and the Jacobian singularity.
Industrial camera sensors and optics: CMOS versus CCD, global and rolling shutters, pixel size, Nyquist resolution, focal length, f-number, telecentric lenses, and GenICam.
2D image processing: color space conversion, histograms and contrast equalization, global, Otsu and adaptive thresholding, contours, moments, blobs, Canny edge detection, and template matching.
3D perception: direct sensing versus 2D inference, stereo disparity geometry, PCL point cloud filtering (PassThrough, VoxelGrid, outliers), RANSAC planes, Euclidean clustering, and bin picking.
Build a ROS 2 camera pipeline in Python: sensor_msgs/Image and CameraInfo, optical frames, image_transport, cv_bridge conversion, real-time OpenCV edge processing, and cam2image test images.
From wiring to industrial networks: sinking and sourcing (NPN/PNP), fieldbus history, line, star, ring topologies, cyclic versus acyclic data, and Device Level Ring recovery.
Lab: UR Modbus TCP general-purpose registers, packing handshake bits in URScript, and writing and reading registers from Python with pymodbus (stand-in server, no hardware).
How a mobile robot finds its position, sees obstacles, plans and follows a path, and recovers when stuck, following the open-source Nav2 project.
Four projects with milestones and rubrics: a simulated work cell, ROS 2 pick-and-place with MoveIt 2, a speed-controlled wheel, and an open-source cell monitor.
Capstone project: build a simulated UR5e pick-and-place with ROS 2, MoveIt 2, MoveIt Task Constructor, mock hardware or Gazebo, milestones, tests, and a rubric.
Capstone project: an open-source ROS 2 cell monitor reading robot state, packed Modbus bits, camera checks, maintenance logs, and opening a real pull request.
